# ethereum-optimism/supersim Weekly Report (Aug 2 - 8, 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
This week, development efforts focused on refining environment variable handling for interoperability and addressing stability issues within the testing suite. A significant strategic shift was noted with the closure of long-standing pipeline improvement tasks due to the upcoming deprecation of `op-node`. The team is currently prioritizing the resolution of port collision flakes in acceptance tests to ensure more reliable CI/CD outcomes for the Superchain infrastructure.

## 🛠️ Key Developments

### Interoperability & Configuration
Work this week targeted the reliability of cross-chain messaging configurations.
*   **Environment Variable Matching:** A fix was initiated to address a bug where the `SUPERSIM_INTEROP_L2TOL2CDM_OVERRIDE` environment variable was not being correctly recognized by the system ([#423](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/supersim/pull/423)). This ensures that developers can accurately override Layer 2 to Layer 2 Cross-Domain Messenger settings during simulation.

## 🐛 Issues & Triage

### Closed Issues
*   **Pipeline Improvements & Deprecation:** The "Holocene-D: Pipeline improvements tracker" ([#12490](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/supersim/issues/12490)) was closed as "not planned." This decision stems from the planned deprecation of `op-node`, rendering previous todos and technical debt within that specific component obsolete as the architecture evolves.

### New & Active Issues
*   **Metrics Port Collisions:** A new high-priority flake was identified in the `op-acceptance-tests` suite ([#22299](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/supersim/issues/22299)). The `kona-sp1-proposer` has been intermittently failing to boot due to "Address already in use" errors on the metrics server port. This issue has been observed across multiple jobs, including `memory-all-kona-op-reth-prague`, and represents a potential blocker for stable deployments on the `develop` branch.

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
The week's activity highlights active maintenance and architectural pivoting. The closure of the pipeline tracker ([#12490](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/supersim/issues/12490)) involved coordination between contributors `sebastianst` and `ajsutton`, reflecting a consensus on the project's long-term technical direction regarding `op-node`. Additionally, the rapid identification and confirmation of test flakes by contributors like `claude` demonstrate a proactive approach to maintaining the health of the Superchain's testing infrastructure.
